observation_summary: SerializationUtils.clone() fails with a ClassNotFoundException when attempting to clone primitive types (e.g., int.class) because the custom ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream does not correctly resolve primitive class names.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves implementing a lookup mechanism for primitive types within the resolveClass method of ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream. This is a procedural correction to the class resolution algorithm, ensuring that primitive class names are correctly mapped to their corresponding Class objects when standard class loading fails. It is not a simple guard (Checking) or a single value initialization (Assignment/Initialization), but a refinement of the resolution logic.
evidence_used: The bug report states that the problem is that the custom resolveClass method does not handle primitive types correctly.
The fix diff shows the addition of a primitiveTypes map and logic to check this map when Class.forName fails.
The stack trace shows a ClassNotFoundException for 'byte' during serialization.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds checks (if/else), the core issue is the absence of a lookup algorithm for primitive types, which is a procedural requirement for the class resolution method.
The fix initializes a map, but the primary purpose of the change is to alter the resolution algorithm, not just to initialize a variable.
